title: Training a logistic regression
sub: Gradient descent on the cross-entropy loss, in two dimensions.

frames.caption: Two overlapping classes. The model is p(class 1 | x) = σ(w·x + b). The solid green line is where p = 0.5, the decision boundary; the dashed lines are where p = 0.1 and 0.9. We start from a poor guess.
Each gradient step moves w by the average of (p − y)·x: points that are misclassified, or classified with too little confidence, pull hardest.
The boundary turns into place. The dashed lines are far apart: the classes overlap, so the model stays honestly uncertain near the middle.
Converged. Loss 0.084, accuracy 97%. Because the classes overlap, the cross-entropy has a genuine minimum, and the weights settle at |w| = 4.68.
Now two classes that a line can separate perfectly.
Accuracy hits 100% quickly. But the loss keeps falling, because it can always be lowered further by making the predictions more confident.
And the only way to be more confident is a bigger w. The p = 0.1 and p = 0.9 lines squeeze together around the boundary: |w| = 7.0.

|w| = 8.6 and still growing: the loss approaches 0 but never reaches a minimum, because the maximum-likelihood estimate does not exist for separable data. In practice the fix is regularization (an L2 penalty gives a finite optimum) or early stopping.
